definitions:
em_e4recon_assemble.py (tag e4recon): assemble the FINAL error-mode numbers for the paper.

Reads (local):
  data/leakage/em_e4recon_analysis.json   (em_e4recon_analyze.py on graham; per-bit counts/variances for every model)
  data/leakage/em_e1hmm_results.json      (robustness: HMM state change, Gaussian overlap at the CNN surrogate)
  data/leakage/em_e2seg_results.json      (robustness: alpha/null variants, efficiency-corrected shares, Gaussian MF/proxy)
  data/leakage/em_e3herq_summary_v3.json  (HERQULES error rates / co-failure, for cross-reference)
Writes:
  data/leakage/em_e4recon_final.json

Final per-error accounting (count level, per qubit and prepared bit, then summed):
  N = L + T + O + S
  L = leakage (line-frame E3 flag z > 3 minus mirror z < -3)                    MEASURED (k = 3 lower bound)
  T = resolved mid-readout transition (e2seg v3 GLRT, alpha = 0.01, FP-corrected, gated)  MEASURED lower bound
  O = near-boundary overlap = min(R, late-core expectation), R = N - L - T         MEASURED upper bound
      late-core expectation = sum_cfg N(b,cfg) * P(model error | prepared b, cfg, late window 1-2 us in |b> core)
  S = R - O = no resolved event, in excess of overlap                              MEASURED lower bound (by elimination)
      identity INFERRED: qubit in the other computational state for most of the window (transition before
      ~150-250 ns or before the window, preparation/thermal error); supported by the late-window confirmation.
  State change (relaxation/excitation before or during the readout) = T + S = N - L - O   (independent of the step detector)
CIs: var(L) = N+ + N-; var(T) = flags + MC var(FP sum); var(O) = binomial per cfg; var(S) = var(L)+var(T)+var(O);
     var(T+S) = var(L) + var(O); if O is capped at R then O = R, S = 0, var(O) = var(L) + var(T).

herqules.co_failure_from_e3herq: 68.2% [67.9, 68.5] of per-trace HERQULES Q3 errors and 92.1% [91.8, 92.4] of Q5 errors are also CNN errors (1 us); 75.5% / 80.5% at 400 ns (e3herq, MEASURED)

robustness_notes.order_swap: transition before leakage: residual / overlap / unresolved state change move by <= 0.03 pp on every qubit; only the L/T split moves (Q3 L 3.14 -> 1.70 %, T 1.75 -> 3.18 %; Q5 L 1.03 -> 0.89 %, T 5.02 -> 5.16 %): 7.7 % of Q3 prepared-|0> errors are both leaked and step-flagged
robustness_notes.soft1000_vs_canonical: same attribution on the soft 1 us model: all shares within 0.6 pp (Q4 overlap +0.62 pp; others <= 0.5 pp) (see windows.1us_cnn_soft1000_crosscheck)
robustness_notes.soft_output_depth_split_rejected: a per-error near-boundary split on the model's own P(correct) (threshold = 5th percentile of P(correct) of the late-core overlap errors, p* = 0.004-0.06) classifies 85-93% of residual errors as 'near' although the count-level late-core expectation allows only 4-12% of prepared-|1> errors on Q1/Q3/Q5: the CNN is NOT confident on early-decay traces (it is calibrated against decays), so model confidence is not a near-boundary criterion. This is also why the old P(correct) < 0.6 rule could not separate anything.
robustness_notes.late_core_is_upper_bound: the late-core expectation multiplies the stationary-shot misread rate by ALL prepared-b shots (incl. shots that decayed or leaked inside the window) and its reference set contains a few shots that changed state and came back; O is therefore an upper bound and S / T+S lower bounds. For Q2 (SNR ~1.2) the late core is impure (|0> and |1> late clouds overlap) and O is loose.
robustness_notes.Q4: Q4 leakage and transitions are n/m (multimodal |1>: a stationary reduced-shift sub-cloud holds ~21% of prepared |1>); errors on that sub-cloud fall outside the late-core reference and are counted in S, so Q4's S is not purely state change.
robustness_notes.Q2: overlap-dominated in every estimate: late core 98.5% (upper), e2seg near-Bayes Gaussian >= observed count, e1hmm Gaussian at the CNN surrogate 58%; e1hmm's 51% HMM state change for Q2 is not credible (15% false-alarm rate on stationary prepared-|1> shots).

criteria.source: Oraqle/Discriminators/runners/_train_and_analyze_hybridcnn.py (per-shot categories) + herqules_error_report.py (aggregation into herqules_error_breakdown_hybridcnn.csv, 1000 ns rows -> tab:error_modes)
criteria.model: HybridCNN (not MCMit-CNN), sparse-FIR demod (HERQULES IFs, 101-tap Hamming 5 MHz LPF, every DS-th sample; DS=40 at 1 us, T_ds=13; the 400 ns checkpoint matches only with DS=20, T_ds=10)
criteria.near_boundary: P(correct) < 0.60 from the model's own sigmoid output: true for EVERY error (an error has P(correct) < 0.5)
criteria.t1_relaxation: Wiener envelope env = mean(x0-x1)/var(x0-x1) on flattened [I,Q] demod (TRAIN, random equal-size pairing, RandomState(0)); mf1/mf2 = projections of the first/second half of the window (raw, no offset subtracted); flag if |mf1| > 0.5 median|mf1| and |mf2| > 0.5 median|mf2| over all TEST shots and sign(mf1) != sign(mf2)
criteria.leakage_column: amp outlier: |z| > 3 with z = (time-mean |IQ| of the demod - TRAIN mean)/TRAIN std pooled over both states; labelled 'Excitation' by herqules_error_report.py and 'Leakage' in the paper
criteria.priority: t1 > amp > near > other (other always empty because near covers every error)
criteria.why_t1_is_not_a_transition_test: the sign of a raw (un-centred) projection is not a state indicator: on Q1 and Q3 both prepared states give the same sign in both halves (Q3: frac mf>0 = 0 for both), so the test can never fire; on Q5 prepared |0> has frac(mf1>0) = 0.25 vs frac(mf2>0) = 0.75, so 9.5% of ALL prepared-|0> shots are 'T1' flagged (prepared |1>: 1.4%); counts follow the IQ-origin geometry, not transitions

old_method.verified_in_source_by_e4recon: Oraqle/Discriminators/runners/_train_and_analyze_hybridcnn.py l.28-29 (NEAR_THR=0.60, AMP_Z=3), l.48-56 (_mf_envelope = mean(z-o)/var(z-o), RandomState(0) pairing), l.146-171 (conf<0.6; amp z vs pooled TRAIN mean/std; mf1/mf2 un-centred halves, |mf|>0.5 median, sign(mf1)!=sign(mf2); priority t1 > amp > near)
